newsitem.title: UK: MPs torpedo British Conservative rally plan.
newsitem.headline: MPs torpedo British Conservative rally plan.

text.p: Senior ministers' efforts to unite ruling Conservatives for an imminent British election were torpedoed on Friday by MPs speculating about leadership battles if they lost.

While one of the party's legislators urged Prime Minister John Major to step down as party leader immediately after an election defeat, another urged him to stay on, saying some of his potential successors could lose their seats.
The comments coincided with party members gathering in the western English city of Bath for a rally designed to give them new heart for the electoral battle.

While finance minister Kenneth Clarke delivered a stinging attack on Labour's economic spokesman Gordon Brown for indecisiveness, former minister Edwina Currie was speculating on BBC radio about what would happen in the aftermath of a defeat.
Currie said manoeuvring ahead of a leadership contest was already under way.
"There is already a great deal of formation of columns and lines and factions and groups," she said.

She said a leadership contest to clear the air if Labour came to power would be vital. "Please, John, please don't make us hang around," Currie said. "Please don't make us wait. Can we please get on with it."
But another MP, John Biffen, told the same programme the Conservative's defeat could be so great that senior cabinet members who might fight such a contest would lose their seats.
"There might then be a case to wait until by-elections can be held to remedy that situation," he said.
The open speculation among Tories about defeat came within seven weeks of the expected May 1 date of a general election, and after a newspaper poll showed Labour 25 points ahead of the Conservatives.
It overshadowed Clarke's speech in which he said Britain would take a holiday from economic history if it elects a Labour government.
Clarke said that under Labour, Britain would turn its back on the liberalising economic approach which was starting to make it a role model for the world.
"Who knows what they might get from Labour? Do you expect tough decisions from people who refuse to answer any straight questions?" he said.
Headded that it was plain that Labour had announced it would have a budget in July if it won power because it intended to raise taxes -- something Brown has consistently denied.
Clarke mocked Brown for having promised to keep income tax rates at present levels in government, and to maintain the levels of public spending the Conservatives have proposed for the next two years.
"Gordon, you can put on a Liverpool football shirt if you want, but it won't make you Robbie Fowler," he joked. "You can put on a mini-skirt, but it won't make you a Spice Girl.
"The public should realise -- if you vote Labour, you won't get Conservative policies. There is no option marked "Tory policies, Labour men".

"If you vote Labour, you call a halt to tax-cutting, you vote for higher spending, you give more powers to the (trade) unions...voting. Labour means an end to the economic reform agenda which has transformed Britain from basket-case to role model."

An opinion poll in the Indepedent newspaper was gloomy reading for the Conservative faithful in Bath. It showed the party's support at just 27 percent of the electorate, against 52 percent for Labour.
